newsitem.title: JAPAN: No move on coalition until votes counted-Hashimoto.
newsitem.headline: No move on coalition until votes counted-Hashimoto.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said he would not start discussing forming a new coalition government until the final results of Sunday's general election were known.

Asked whether his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) was considering forming a coalition government, he told NHK public television: "When the results (of the elections) are clear, I expect we will start discussing this issue with the other parties."
But Hashimoto refused to be drawn on which parties he was considering as possible coalition partners.
"Regardless of...party, we would of course consider cooperation with people who would say to us 'Let's take on this future era of change together'," he said without elaborating.
Earlier, senior LDP officials had said it would be difficult for the party to win a simple majority in the election for the 500-member Lower House.
Hashimoto's LDP was the dominant partner in the outgoing coalition government, which included the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake, an LDP splinter group.
